plates.table: Ambrogio 1539: the 22 characters which, he reports, Raziel says the angel Raphiel gave written to Adam (no heading; introduced 'Quarum quidem literarum figurae, & nomina sunt infrascripta, videlicet.'). This is the alphabet Duret 1613 heads 'Characteres de l'Ange Raphael' and Mathers 1889 (Plate XV) heads 'Alphabet of the Magi'. Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale di Roma copy.
plates.layout: 3 rows read RIGHT to LEFT in Hebrew order, each Latin-letter Hebrew name printed UNDER its sign. Row 1: 8 signs (Aleph at far right ... Hhet at far left). Row 2: 8 signs (Teth ... Ain). Row 3: 6 signs (Phe ... Thau), right-aligned, followed at the LEFT by a printed point and a fleuron, which are space-fillers and carry no label. 22 signs in all; no final forms.

source.work: The Key of Solomon the King (Clavicula Salomonis), now first translated and edited from ancient MSS in the British Museum
source.author: S. Liddell MacGregor Mathers (ed., tr.)
source.edition: First edition, limited to 500 numbered copies (Wellcome MARC 500). Wellcome MARC 300 gives 'viii, 114 pages, xv leaves of plates', but this copy also has a p. 115 ('The Qabalistical Invocation of Solomon', ending 'THE END', n156) after p. 114 ('(HERE ENDETH THE FRAGMENT OF THE KEY OF SOLOMON.)'): the record and the copy disagree by that page.
source.date: 1889 (title page: 'LONDON / GEORGE REDWAY / YORK STREET COVENT GARDEN / 1889', as read in this copy's OCR text b24884431_djvu.txt and in the Wellcome MARC 260); the preface is signed 'S. LIDDELL MACGREGOR MATHERS. London, October, 1888.' (same OCR text; checked).
source.copy: Wellcome Collection, London (record b24884431; print record b1542215x; archive.org shelfmark field 'BVA.CA'); Wellcome library stamp on p. 114.
source.image_index: n154 (0-based BookReader index; scandata leafNum 155, because leaf 0 is excluded from the access images). n155 is the blank verso of the plate.
source.printed_locator: Plate XV (unpaginated plate leaf). The 'Directions to Binder' leaf (n157) places Plate XV 'At the end of the book'; in this copy it is bound between p. 114 (n153) and p. 115 (n156).
source.rights: archive.org rights field: 'This work is available under the Creative Commons, Public Domain Mark' (http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/); contributor/sponsor Wellcome Library.

legibility: 1539 BNCR (colour, 1880 px page): every sign and label complete and sharp; faint show-through of the ring-letter alphabets printed on fol. 203v sits behind the signs (grey, distinguishable from the black print). 1539 LOC (grayscale, 3790 px spread): same signs, slightly heavier inking, crisp labels, faint show-through. The two copies agree sign for sign, including the dots, the point and the fleuron, so the table is printed (not added by hand) in both. 1613 Duret: microfiche, high-contrast and specky but every sign and italic label is legible. 1889 Mathers: clean lithographed plate on blue paper; all forms legible.
problems: The archive.org IIIF image server still answered HTTP 504 for n409 at check time; the BNCR crop is now cut directly from the jp2 master (fetched singly from bub_gb_yUkKq_QnrnwC_jp2.zip), so it no longer carries the extra JPEG generation of the page/n409.jpg derivative.

Free dots belong to several signs (Aleph, Hhet, Teth, Iod at right; Lamed has a colon-like pair; Samech a dot inside). They appear identically in both 1539 copies and should be traced as part of the forms. The point and fleuron at the left of row 3 are space-fillers, not letters.
LOC copy only: a small slanting tick after the Hhet sign (absent in BNCR); treat as an accidental mark unless a third copy shows it.
Teth's tail descends into the label line, between 'Iod.' and 'Teth.' — the curl is part of the sign, not of the label.
BNCR shelfmark not confirmed (labels '6 | 11 K | 5' and pencil '6-1.d.14' on the pastedown).
Only the March issue ('Kal. Martij') was seen, in both copies; the April issue reported by ADER was not found or compared.

Checker: both 1539 crops as first cut clipped the label row at the bottom (the descender of the 'p' in 'Coph.' by c. 10 px in both copies; in BNCR also the last c. 3 px of the point after 'Phe.'); re-cut taller (BNCR 1440x638 -> 1440x650, LOC 1300x550 -> 1300x562, same origins), so the strips now include the tops of the next text line.
Duret 1613: several label points are not visible on the fiche (see copy_note on Hheth, Vau, Daleth, Beth, Caph, Iod).
notes: First printing confirmed on the page: Ambrogio, Introductio, Pavia 1539, fol. 203r. Labels as printed, right to left: 'Hhet. Zain. Vau. He. Daleth. Gimel. Beth. Aleph.' / 'Ain. Samech. Nun. Mem. Lamed. Caph. Iod. Teth.' / 'Thau. Sin. Res. Coph. Zadai. Phe.' — exactly 22 signs, no finals, every label in its Hebrew place; nothing is paired with an unexpected letter.

TEXT AROUND THE TABLE (transcribed from the BNCR scan, fols. 202v-203r; normalised: long s to s, æ to ae ('Adae', 'figurae'), e caudata to e ('preciosis', printed 'pręciosis'), accent dropped in 'sanè'; abbreviations 'Angelũ' and 'atqꝫ' expanded to 'Angelum', 'atque'; the catchword 'inuentas' at the foot of 202v is not repeated): 'In secundo quippe tractatu, in quo de lapidibus preciosis loquitur Raziel, reprobata illorum opinione qui dicunt, viginti duas literas, de quibus ibi loquitur, à Camaliele fuisse inuentas. Angelum Raphiel, in libro qui dicitur liber ignis, illas Adae Protoplasto dedisse scriptas asseuerat, & ob id filios Adam eas recusare non posse. Quarum quidem literarum figurae, & nomina sunt infrascripta, videlicet.' After the table: 'Posuit autem ibidem Raziel, dictarum literarum interpretationem, atque virtutem, alio prorsus quam beatus Hieronymus, & diuerso posuerit modo, de qua sane expositione, nullam omnino faciendam esse curam censeo.' OWN PARAPHRASE (not a published translation): In the second treatise [of the Raziel book], where Raziel speaks of precious stones, he rejects the opinion of those who say that the twenty-two letters he discusses there were invented by Camaliel; he asserts that the angel Raphiel, in the book called the Book of Fire, gave them to Adam the first-made man in writing, so that Adam's sons cannot refuse them. Their shapes and names follow. Raziel also gives an interpretation and power of the letters quite different from St Jerome's, which Ambrogio says need not be heeded. (Whether 'in libro qui dicitur liber ignis' goes with Raziel's assertion or with Raphiel's gift is grammatically open; Duret 1613, p. 117, reads it as a second place where Raziel says this: 'au second traité de ses institutions ... & au liure intitulé du feu'.)

The source Ambrogio names is the Raziel book among the manuscripts of Antonio de Fantis of Treviso that he says he read and excerpted (fol. 202v: '... memini me vidisse opera, Razielis, Picatricis, Bailum, Mercurij, Petri Apponis, Salomonis, ac interpretis illius Apollonij ...').

The table that follows on the same page (fol. 203r, lower) is a DIFFERENT alphabet, introduced 'Ex varijs praeterea qui Solomoni attribuuntur libris, & interprete eius Apollonio infrascriptos literarum characteres ... desumpsimus' (labels 'Hheth ... Aleph', 'Ain ... Lamech ... Ioth ... Teth', 'Thau. Sin. Res. Coph. Sade. Phe.'). Do not crop or trace it as the Alphabet of the Magi. The Apollonius connection in Ambrogio belongs to this second table, not to the Raphiel alphabet.

Identity check: Mathers' 'Alphabet of the Magi' column (Plate XV) gives the same signs in the same Hebrew assignments as Ambrogio's Raphiel table for almost every letter, and Duret 1613 p. 117 gives them under 'Characteres de l'Ange Raphael' citing 'Theseus Ambrosius'. Mathers agrees with Duret, not Ambrogio, at Yod (hooked reversed C with dot) and Shin (S inside the U), so Mathers' plate descends through Duret or a Duret-derived chart, not directly from the 1539 cut.

Voarchadumia checked: Pantheus, Voarchadumia contra alchimiam, Venice: Giovanni Tacuino, April 1530 (Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale di Firenze, Magl. 1.6.584; archive.org ita-bnc-mag-00001097-001, images n35-n41, fols. 12r-15r) prints four alphabets: the common square Hebrew, the 'Moses on Sinai' characters (square Hebrew forms), the 'transitu fluuii ... Abrae' characters (fol. 14r) and the Enoch alphabet keyed to A-Z (fols. 14v-15r). None is the Raphiel / Magi alphabet. Ambrogio himself (fol. 202r) lists exactly these four from Pantheus. The images there carry 'Copyright © 2011 ProQuest LLC' (Early European Books) and no archive.org license, so no plate was saved from them.
Use the 1539 BNCR crop as the tracing master (colour, sharp); check every sign against the LOC crop.
